en.title: Wishes and hypotheses
en.summary: Wish, if only and suppose express wishes and imagined situations.

paragraphs: We use wish and if only to express regret about a situation that is not as we would like, and suppose or imagine to ask about hypothetical situations. In each case the verb moves one step back in time: the past form refers to the present, and the past perfect to the past.

blocks.html:
MeaningPatternExample
regret about nowwish + past simpleI wish I lived by the sea.
regret about the pastwish + past perfectI wish I had studied more.
annoyance or wish for changewish + wouldI wish he would stop talking.
stronger feelingif only + same formsIf only I knew the answer!

paragraphs: Use wish + would for something that annoys you and that someone else could change. Do not use it with I or we for yourself. For ability, use wish + could: I wish I could swim.

blocks.html:
CorrectIncorrect
I wish it would stop raining.I wish I would win.
I wish I could help.I wish I can help.
I wish she were here.I wish she is here.

paragraphs: Suppose, supposing, imagine and what if introduce an imagined situation. The verb forms follow the pattern of the second and third conditional: Suppose you lost your job? What if we had missed the train?

items: Wrong: **I wish I have more money.** Right: **I wish I had more money.**
Wrong: **I wish I would be taller.** Right: **I wish I were taller.**
Wrong: **If only I would know!** Right: **If only I knew!**
